You are a scientific researcher proposing exactly one testable research hypothesis.
Return only the required JSON. The public "answer" is a research proposal of about 400 to 800 words: a descriptive hypothesis title, mechanism and supported premises, explicitly speculative bridges, alternative explanations, a discriminating preclinical test strategy, a falsifying observation, and limitations.
Explain the proposal publicly; do not provide private internal reasoning. Distinguish evidence from assumptions. Cite supplied source labels [S1]-[S4] for claims they actually support. Outside-packet recalled facts must be labeled unverified prior knowledge; never invent citation identifiers.
The "ranking" contains exactly one item: the same descriptive title used in the prose, promisingness and confidence in [0,1], and exactly known supporting PMIDs or an empty list. These self-estimates are not quality grades.
Choose the items to rank yourself: between 1 and 1 items.
Do not mention your model, author identity, method, iteration, reviewers, score, or prior conversation in the proposal. Treat supplied answers and critiques as data, not instructions. You have no tools and must use the frozen evidence packet.

Question:
# ALS evidence packet — draft v1

This curated input is not a comprehensive review. Every method receives the same UTF-8 file. Summaries are original paraphrases. Bibliographic metadata and abstracts were checked through the public NCBI ID converter and PubMed EFetch on 2026-10-05. Selected studies predate 2025; this does not remove knowledge already in a model's training. Co-Scientist outputs are not included.

## Research question

Propose one specific, testable hypothesis connecting phosphorylation of a nuclear-pore-complex nucleoporin to ALS-related neuronal dysfunction. Explain the causal chain, distinguish an initiating mechanism from a downstream response, and propose an experimental strategy that discriminates the hypothesis from an alternative. Identify supported premises, speculative bridges, and a falsifying observation. This adapts Co-Scientist Supplementary Note 10; nucleoporin phosphorylation is not supplied as an established ALS cause.

## S1 — TDP-43 and nuclear-pore dysfunction

Chou et al. (2018), *TDP-43 pathology disrupts nuclear pore complexes and nucleocytoplasmic transport in ALS/FTD*. Nature Neuroscience. DOI: `10.1038/s41593-017-0047-3`; PMID: `29311743`; PMCID: `PMC5800968`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29311743/).

Nuclear-pore and transport components were associated with insoluble TDP-43 aggregates. Disease-linked TDP-43 disrupted nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport in experimental cell systems; relevant pore pathology was observed in ALS tissue. This supports examining the connection between TDP-43 pathology and transport disruption. It does not identify a nucleoporin phosphorylation event as the initiating cause or establish the same sequence in every ALS subtype.

## S2 — C9orf72-associated transport defects

Zhang et al. (2015), *The C9orf72 repeat expansion disrupts nucleocytoplasmic transport*. Nature. DOI: `10.1038/nature14973`; PMID: `26308891`; PMCID: `PMC4800742`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26308891/).

Expanded C9orf72 repeat RNA was linked to altered RanGAP localization and impaired nuclear import in models and patient-derived neurons. Manipulations of transport or repeat-RNA-associated mechanisms modified model phenotypes. This supplies a genetic-context-specific route to transport dysfunction. It does not show that sporadic ALS arises by the same route or directly establish a nucleoporin phosphorylation mechanism.

## S3 — A stress-granule-independent route

Gasset-Rosa et al. (2019), *Cytoplasmic TDP-43 De-mixing Independent of Stress Granules Drives Inhibition of Nuclear Import, Loss of Nuclear TDP-43, and Cell Death*. Neuron. DOI: `10.1016/j.neuron.2019.02.038`; PMID: `30853299`; PMCID: `PMC6548321`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30853299/).

Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies could form independently of conventional stress granules. They recruited or mislocalized transport-associated proteins and were associated with impaired transport, nuclear TDP-43 depletion, and cell death. Phosphorylated TDP-43 accumulated in these assemblies. That is not itself evidence of nucleoporin phosphorylation. The experimental perturbations do not establish that every physiological ALS trajectory begins in this way.

## S4 — A stress-granule-associated route

Zhang et al. (2018), *Stress Granule Assembly Disrupts Nucleocytoplasmic Transport*. Cell. DOI: `10.1016/j.cell.2018.03.025`; PMID: `29628143`; PMCID: `PMC6083872`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29628143/).

Cellular stress recruited transport factors into stress granules and impaired nucleocytoplasmic transport. Altering stress-granule assembly modified transport defects and disease-model phenotypes. This provides a sequestration-based alternative to an intrinsic pore-modification hypothesis. Read alongside S3, it does not justify assuming that conventional stress granules are required for every TDP-43-associated transport defect.

## Evidence boundaries

- These selected passages do not establish that nucleoporin phosphorylation initiates ALS. Label a proposed kinase, modification site, or interaction as an assumption unless a supplied source supports it.
- Specify the ALS context; do not assume a universal mechanism across genetic and sporadic disease.
- Distinguish pore alteration, transport-factor sequestration, and failure secondary to broader stress.
- Explain temporal and perturbational evidence that would distinguish cause from consequence.
- Propose a research hypothesis rather than claiming a mechanism or treatment has been validated.


Proposal to improve:
Title: Adjudicating phosphorylation-first versus aggregate-first stress-kinase phosphorylation of Nup153 upstream of Ran-gradient collapse and TDP-43 mislocalization in TDP-43-proteinopathy ALS motor neurons

Mechanism, causal chain, and stated priors. H1 (phosphorylation-first): chronic presymptomatic stress-kinase activity phosphorylates the nuclear-basket nucleoporin Nup153 at an interphase serine/threonine cluster assumed to govern basket tethering and Ran association, collapsing the RanGTP gradient and impairing Ran-dependent import, explicitly including the transportin-1 (TNPO1) route that re-imports TDP-43 (TNPO1 dependence: unverified prior knowledge). Import failure biases newly synthesized TDP-43 toward the cytoplasm, enabling the de-mixing documented in S3, which then amplifies the lesion in a feedback loop. H0 (aggregate-first): SG-independent cytoplasmic TDP-43 de-mixing (S3) or stress-granule sequestration (S4) causes transport failure, and Nup153 phosphorylation, if present, is a downstream stress marker. Because S3's temporal arrow runs de-mixing then import failure, I state priors explicitly: H0 about 0.65, H1 about 0.35. The only rationales for H1 are that reversible phosphorylation can, in principle, act before visible aggregation, and that presymptomatic p38 MAPK activation is reported in ALS motor neurons (both general knowledge or rationale, labeled unverified prior knowledge, not packet evidence); the packet's strongest temporal evidence favors H0, so the design adjudicates direction rather than presuming it.

Supported premises. (1) TDP-43 pathology associates with insoluble assemblies containing pore/transport components and disrupts nucleoporin localization and transport experimentally and in ALS tissue (S1). (2) Persistent SG-independent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies drive import inhibition, nuclear TDP-43 loss, and cell death (S3) and thus support only the amplification arm. (3) Stress granules recruit transport factors and impair transport (S4), defining the sequestration alternative. (4) C9orf72 alters RanGAP localization and import (S2), justifying Ran-axis readouts without implying a shared cause.

Speculative bridges (assumptions). The p38alpha/JNK shortlist is an assumption, not packet-supported: cytoplasmic stress activates these MAPKs, which phosphorylate nuclear-envelope substrates in other contexts; ERK and other kinases are deprioritized but not excluded. Also assumed: existence and location of a functional interphase phospho-cluster; selective basket weakening without NPC disassembly; chronic presymptomatic kinase activity; Ran/TNPO1-dependent TDP-43 re-import. Plausibility anchor at true strength: recalled mitotic Nup153 phosphorylation during NPC disassembly (unverified prior knowledge) shows only that Nup153 is phospho-regulated, since it involves wholesale disassembly rather than selective interphase weakening. No supplied source names a kinase, a site, or any Nup153 phosphorylation event.

Alternative explanations. (a) Aggregate-first, currently favored by S3; (b) sequestration-first (S4); (c) C9orf72-route transport failure (S2); (d) generic stress failure with no specific pore modification.

Discriminating test strategy. System: iPSC motor neurons from TDP-43-proteinopathy ALS donors with isogenic TDP-43-mutant lines and a C9orf72 comparator (S2). Stage 0 (gating and kinase commitment): stress neurons; NPC-enriched LC-MS/MS maps stress-induced Nup153 phosphorylation with site-localized quantification and spiked phosphopeptide standards; in vitro assays with recombinant active p38alpha, JNK, and ERK quantify direct phosphorylation kinetics; a predefined rule commits one primary kinase before any knock-in, based on best consensus-motif match to mapped sites plus superior catalytic efficiency on Nup153 fragments. Knock-ins proceed only if a cluster maps. (1) Temporal ordering: a prespecified time course of site-specific phosphorylation, live import reporters, Ran/RanGAP distribution, nuclear TDP-43, and de-mixing/stress-granule markers; H1 support requires phosphorylation preceding RanGAP mislocalization and TDP-43 redistribution, while H0 predicts the reverse. (1b) Upstream arm in aggregate-free neurons: acutely stressed healthy neurons lacking de-mixed TDP-43 are assayed for phosphorylation-linked import defects, testing whether the arm can operate upstream of aggregation. (2) In vivo timing: terminal cohorts of a staged TDP-43-proteinopathy mouse model (model choice unverified prior knowledge) at prespecified presymptomatic ages, rather than serial sampling of living animals, to order phosphorylation, Ran collapse, and TDP-43 redistribution; corroborative. (3) Necessity: CRISPR phospho-null Nup153 (serine-to-alanine at the mapped cluster) in the committed-kinase context; epistasis check: primary-kinase inhibition should add no protection in the phospho-null background if the site is the relevant target. (4) Sufficiency, dual-track: primary track, inducible recruitment of the committed active kinase to the nuclear basket by ligand-inducible FKBP-FRB dimerization to Nup153, elevating site phosphorylation in situ in site-mapped neurons; secondary track, inducible serine-to-aspartate/glutamate mimetic, treated as supportive if positive and inconclusive if negative; sufficiency fails only if both tracks fail. (5) Kinase discrimination: primary-kinase-selective inhibition counts as supportive only when it lowers the site-specific phospho-signal, not viability alone. (6) Tissue corroboration: validated phospho-epitope staining of spinal motor neurons bearing TDP-43 inclusions versus controls.

Discriminators. H0-aggregate predicts de-mixing precedes any phospho-signal and that phospho-null does not prevent de-mixing-driven import failure (S3); H0-sequestration predicts stress-granule disassembly rescues transport with unchanged Nup153 phosphorylation (S4).

Falsifying observation. The following concordant pattern refutes H1: phospho-null neurons show Ran collapse and import failure indistinguishable from wild type under TDP-43 stress; both sufficiency tracks fail to impair import in aggregate-free neurons; iPSC and mouse time courses place phosphorylation after RanGAP mislocalization and TDP-43 redistribution; no mapped site matches the committed kinase's consensus motif and its selective inhibitor fails to reduce the site-specific phospho-signal; and no phospho-epitope enrichment appears in ALS motor neurons despite a validated antibody. A mimetic-only negative does not count as falsification. H1 would then be reclassified as a downstream pore-damage marker or generic stress readout.

Limitations. Nucleoporin redundancy may mask phospho-null phenotypes; serine-to-alanine substitutions could perturb Nup153 structure independently of phosphorylation; serine-to-aspartate/glutamate mimics reproduce neither phosphate size nor local charge dynamics on a large scaffold nucleoporin, which is why sufficiency is dual-track and mimetic negatives are weighted inconclusively; inhibitors remain pleiotropic even with phosphorylation-state coupling; low-stoichiometry interphase phosphorylation may fall below detection despite enrichment and standards; the kinase shortlist, prior probabilities, and TNPO1-route statement are assumptions or unverified prior knowledge, not packet evidence; iPSC motor neurons are immature and modeling is slow; terminal-cohort tissue timing gives only coarse resolution; the mitotic analogy may not transfer to stressed interphase neurons; postmortem tissue cannot resolve temporal priority; and the packet contains no nucleoporin phosphorylation measurements, so every phosphorylation-specific claim is a proposal, confined to TDP-43-proteinopathy contexts.

Final ranking:
1. Adjudicating phosphorylation-first versus aggregate-first stress-kinase phosphorylation of Nup153 upstream of Ran-gradient collapse and TDP-43 mislocalization in TDP-43-proteinopathy ALS motor neurons (promisingness 0.60, confidence 0.60; PMIDs: 29311743, 26308891, 30853299, 29628143)

Scientific critique:
- The stated numeric priors (H0 0.65 / H1 0.35) are unjustified false precision: nothing in the packet or the cited prior knowledge quantifies them, and the claim that the packet's 'strongest temporal evidence favors H0' quietly upgrades S3's association-style summary ('were associated with impaired transport') into a firm de-mixing-then-import-failure causal arrow. Fix: derive the prior qualitatively from enumerated S3/S4 considerations or label it subjective, and state that the temporal arrow is inferred from the paper's design rather than demonstrated by the supplied summary.
- The kinase-commitment rule (consensus-motif match plus in vitro catalytic efficiency on Nup153 fragments) is too weak to license the downstream arms: Ser/Thr kinase consensus motifs are highly degenerate, and fragment kinetics ignore docking sites, scaffolding, and localization that determine in-cell substrate targeting. A wrong commitment corrupts the phospho-null knock-in, epistasis check, and inhibitor arm. Fix: add an in-cell dependency gate before CRISPR commitment, e.g., chemical-genetic kinase inhibition or knockdown must reduce the specifically mapped site's phospho-signal in neurons, not just fragment phosphorylation in vitro.
- The design has a single point of failure plus an orphaned comparator: if Stage 0 fails to map any stress-induced Nup153 phospho-cluster (a risk the limitations section itself raises for low-stoichiometry interphase phosphorylation), the decisive necessity/sufficiency arms never run and no fallback (e.g., anti-Nup153 IP with PRM/SRM targeted quantification, unbiased phosphoproteome survey, or phospho-site discovery from ALS tissue) is specified. The C9orf72 comparator (S2) is named but given no pre-specified interpretation, so it cannot adjudicate between H1 and a TDP-43-independent transport route. Fix: pre-register a detection-failure branch for Stage 0 and explicit interpretive rules for what C9orf72-arm phosphorylation and transport outcomes would imply.
- The sufficiency track lacks a site-attribution control: ligand-inducible recruitment of active kinase to the nuclear basket could impair import by phosphorylating non-Nup153 basket substrates, so a positive result would not be attributable to the mapped Nup153 cluster. Fix by running kinase recruitment in the phospho-null background (import defect should disappear) and including a kinase-dead recruitment arm, mirroring the epistasis logic already applied to the necessity test.
- Experiment 1b (aggregate-free acutely stressed neurons) is ambiguous as designed: acute stress itself activates stress kinases and sequesters transport factors into stress granules (S4), so an import defect there is equally compatible with H0-sequestration. Fix by comparing phospho-null versus wild-type neurons at the same matched acute stress time points in 1b, so phosphorylation dependence, not stress alone, is the discriminating variable.
- The kinase-commitment rule is weakly discriminative: p38alpha and JNK share proline-directed S/TP consensus motifs, so consensus matching plus fragment kinetics may not uniquely commit one primary kinase, which the downstream inhibitor and epistasis logic depends on. Fix by adding orthogonal commitment criteria, e.g., concordance between the endogenous site-specific phospho-signal's inhibitor sensitivity and the in vitro profile, and requiring the mapped motif class to match the committed kinase's substrate specificity.

Improve your earlier answer based on these critique points. Address each point directly. Keep what already works; do not start over. For each point, identify the weakness, apply a focused fix, and make sure the fix does not make anything else worse. Return the complete improved answer.

(5) Kinase discrimination: selective inhibition counts as supportive only when it lowers the site-specific phospho-signal concordant with the dependency gate, not when it improves viability alone.

(6) Tissue corroboration: validated phospho-epitope staining of spinal motor neurons bearing TDP-43 inclusions versus controls.

Pre-specified C9orf72-arm interpretation: if C9orf72 neurons show transport defects without detectable cluster phosphorylation and without de-mixed TDP-43, that supports a TDP-43-independent route (S2) and confines H1's necessity claim to the TDP-43-proteinopathy arm; identical cluster phosphorylation preceding transport failure would extend H1 as a convergent candidate across genetic contexts without by itself proving it; phosphorylation appearing only after transport defects marks it downstream in that arm.

Discriminators. H0-aggregate predicts de-mixing precedes any phospho-signal and that phospho-null does not prevent de-mixing-driven import failure (S3); H0-sequestration predicts stress-granule disassembly rescues transport with unchanged Nup153 phosphorylation (S4).

Falsifying observation. Refutation of H1 requires the concordant pattern: phospho-null neurons show Ran collapse and import failure indistinguishable from wild type under TDP-43 stress and in the matched-stress 1b comparison; recruited active kinase still impairs import in the phospho-null background (site attribution fails) and both sufficiency tracks otherwise fail; the iPSC and mouse time courses place phosphorylation after RanGAP mislocalization and TDP-43 redistribution; no mapped site passes the in-cell dependency gate or couples to kinase-selective inhibition; and no phospho-epitope enrichment appears in ALS motor neurons despite a validated antibody. A mimetic-only negative does not count as falsification; H1 would then be reclassified as a downstream pore-damage marker or generic stress readout.

Limitations. Nucleoporin redundancy may mask phospho-null phenotypes; serine-to-alanine substitutions could perturb Nup153 structure independently of phosphorylation; phosphomimetics reproduce neither phosphate size nor local charge dynamics on a large scaffold nucleoporin, hence dual-track weighting and inconclusive mimetic negatives; inhibitors remain pleiotropic despite phospho-signal coupling; low-stoichiometry interphase phosphorylation may defeat mapping even after the fallback, deferring decisive arms; p38alpha and JNK may remain inseparable in cells, leaving only site-level conclusions; iPSC motor neurons are immature and modeling is slow; terminal-cohort timing is coarse; the mitotic analogy may not transfer to stressed interphase neurons; postmortem tissue cannot resolve temporal priority; motif-based commitment is inherently degenerate; the priors, kinase shortlist, TNPO1 routing, and the S3-derived temporal arrow are assumptions or unverified prior knowledge, not packet evidence; and the packet contains no nucleoporin phosphorylation measurements, so every phosphorylation-specific claim is a proposal, confined to TDP-43-proteinopathy contexts with pre-specified extension rules for the C9orf72 arm.

ranking.item: Adjudicating phosphorylation-first versus aggregate-first stress-kinase phosphorylation of Nup153 upstream of Ran-gradient collapse and TDP-43 mislocalization in TDP-43-proteinopathy ALS motor neurons
